courseTitle: Warm Ups, Mobilisations, Drills and Stretches Library

lessons.title: Static Heel Kick Drill
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Stand tall and kick one heel toward your glutes, keeping knees aligned and torso upright. Alternate legs in a controlled, slow motion to engage hamstrings and improve mobility, then speed up to mimic a faster run cadence, keeping this range of motion.

lessons.title: Mountain Climbers
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion while keeping hips low and core tight. Maintain a steady rhythm and controlled form throughout.

lessons.title: Cross Body Mountain Climbers
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Start in a high plank, hands under shoulders, body straight. Drive one knee diagonally toward the opposite elbow, engaging core and keeping hips low. Return leg to start, then switch sides in a controlled or quick rhythm. Maintain steady breathing and strong plank form.

lessons.title: Plyometric Knee Drives
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Stand tall, drive one knee up explosively toward your chest while hopping on the opposite foot. Land softly and repeat rhythmically, keeping your core engaged and movements powerful.

lessons.title: Squat Jumps
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Start in a squat with feet shoulder-width apart, chest up, and core tight. Explosively jump upward, extending hips and arms, then land softly back into a squat position to repeat.

lessons.title: Double Leg Lateral Hop
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Stand with feet together, then jump sideways as far as comfortable, landing softly with both feet. Immediately hop back to the starting position. Keep your knees slightly bent and core engaged to absorb impact and maintain balance.

lessons.title: Double Leg Ventral Hop
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Stand with feet together, then jump forward as far as comfortable, landing softly on both feet. Keep knees slightly bent and core engaged to absorb impact. Step or hop back to start and repeat.

lessons.title: Quick Steps
categories: Warm ups: Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
Heart Rate Raisers and Movement Patterns
lessons.details: Run along in a line to a metronome, practicing getting a rhythm into your muscle memory!

lessons.title: Quick Full Body Mobilisation (2 mins)
lessons.details: A quick mobilisation pre-strength or pre-run targeting the main joints, to warm up the synovial fluid. Use alongside a heart rate raiser if workout will be intense (i.e. brisk walk, jog or cardio machine in the gym).

lessons.title: Ankle Circles, Knee Circles & Hip Circles
lessons.details: Before your lower body strength session, warm up with ankle circles, knee circles, and hip circles for 2 minutes. These movements mobilize joints, boost circulation, and prepare your body for safer, stronger training.

lessons.title: Ankle Circles
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lift one foot off the ground and slowly rotate your ankle in a circular motion, clockwise and then counterclockwise. Keep movements controlled to improve ankle mobility and stability. Repeat on the other foot.

lessons.title: Heel Walk
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lift your toes off the ground and walk forward on your heels, keeping legs straight and core engaged. Maintain balance and controlled steps to strengthen shins and improve ankle stability.

lessons.title: Dynamic Calf Stretch
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Assume a downward dog position, legs straight. stretch one heel towards the ground, then the other. Repeat in a controlled, rhythmic motion to dynamically stretch the calves. Switch sides after desired reps.

lessons.title: Heel Walk
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lift your toes off the ground and walk forward on your heels, keeping legs straight and core engaged. Maintain balance and controlled steps to strengthen shins and improve ankle stability.

lessons.title: Lunge with Knee Drive and Calf Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Step into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the ground. Drive through the front heel to stand, bringing the back knee up toward your chest, then rise onto the ball of the front foot for a calf raise.

lessons.title: Dynamic Hamstring Stretch
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and step one leg forward, bending down to "shoo the chickens" gently! Engage your core and keep your back upright. Repeat for desired reps, then switch legs to dynamically stretch the hamstrings.

lessons.title: Dynamic Quad Stretch
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and pull one heel toward your glutes, holding briefly. Release and swing the leg forward and back in a controlled motion. Repeat for desired reps, then switch legs to dynamically stretch the quadriceps and hip flexors.

lessons.title: Lunge with Knee Drive
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the ground. Push through your front heel to rise, driving the back knee up explosively toward your chest. Maintain balance and core engagement. Repeat on both sides for strength and stability.

lessons.title: Lateral Leg Swings
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and hold onto a support for balance. Swing one leg side to side in a controlled motion, keeping your core engaged and torso stable. Repeat on the other leg to loosen hips and improve mobility.

lessons.title: Wall Knee Drive Drill (fast)
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Start in a standing position leaning into a wall, with a realistic lean from the ankles mimicking good running posture. Quickly drive one knee up toward your chest, alternating legs in a fast, controlled rhythm. Engage your core and maintain balance throughout.

lessons.title: Banded Prone Knee Drive
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Anchor a resistance around your feet. Lie on your back and drive one banded foot forward toward your chest, keeping core engaged. Return to start with control and repeat before switching sides.

lessons.title: Banded Knee Drive
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Anchor a resistance band on your standing leg and loop it around your active foot. Driving the banded knee upwards while keeping the opposite leg stable. Engage core and glutes, controlling the motion. Maintain balance and steady breathing throughout.

lessons.title: Banded Wall Knee Drive (Slow time)
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand leaning into a wall with a band around your feet, in a position which replicates a runner's lean forwards from the ankles. Slowly drive one knee up toward your chest, pause at the top, then return with control. Alternate legs, focusing on slow, controlled movement to strengthen hip flexors and core stability, speeding up as you gain confidence in the full range of motion.

lessons.title: Banded Knee Drive Foot Switches (wall drill)
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand leaning into a wall with a band around your feet, at a realistic lean forwards from the ankle position. Drive one knee up explosively, quickly switch legs, alternating rapidly. Keep your core tight and posture tall to improve hip flexor speed and coordination.

lessons.title: Lunge with Knee Drive
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the ground. Push through your front heel to rise, driving the back knee up explosively toward your chest. Maintain balance and core engagement. Repeat on both sides for strength and stability.

lessons.title: Banded Knee Drives (static drill)
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall with a resistance band around your feet. Pull one knee toward your chest and hold, keeping your core tight and posture upright. Under control, switch legs to improve hip flexor strength and stability.

lessons.title: Back to Front Leg Swings
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and hold a support for balance. Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion, keeping your torso upright and core engaged. Repeat on the other leg to improve hip mobility and dynamic flexibility.

lessons.title: Torso Rotations (with or without band)
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a band or clasping hands together. Rotate your torso side to side, keeping hips stable and core engaged. Move smoothly and avoid over-rotating to maintain control and proper form.

lessons.title: Banded Overhead Switches
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Hold a resistance band overhead with both hands. Rotate the shoulders backwards so that the band is behind you, then rotate forwards so that the band is in front of you. Repeat in a controlled, rhythmic motion for desired reps.

lessons.title: Band Pull Apart
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Hold a resistance band with both hands at shoulder height, arms extended. Keep core tight and shoulders down. Pull the band apart by moving hands outward, squeezing shoulder blades together. Slowly return to start, maintaining tension in the band and controlled movement throughout the exercise.

lessons.title: Band Pull Together
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Hold a resistance band behind your shoulders with both hands, arms extended outwards. Engage core and keep shoulders down. Pull hands toward each other, squeezing shoulder blades and upper back. Slowly return to start, maintaining tension in the band and controlled, smooth motion throughout the exercise.

lessons.title: Shoulder Roll
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall with arms relaxed at your sides. Slowly roll your shoulders up, back, and down in a circular motion. Repeat several times, then switch direction to release tension and improve mobility.

lessons.title: Back to Front Leg Swings
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and hold a support for balance. Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion, keeping your torso upright and core engaged. Repeat on the other leg to improve hip mobility and dynamic flexibility.

lessons.title: Clamshell
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your side with knees bent and feet stacked. Keep hips steady and core engaged. With feet together, lift the top knee upward, opening like a clamshell, without rotating hips. Pause, then lower with control. Repeat, then switch sides to balance strength.

lessons.title: Inverse Clamshells
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your side with knees bent at 90°, feet together. Keeping knees in contact, lift your top ankle as high as possible without rotating your hips. Lower slowly and repeat. Focus on controlled movement and glute engagement.

lessons.title: Mini-Band Hip Abduction
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Place a mini-band around your legs just above or below the knees, depending on length and strength of band. Stand with hips shoulder width apart. Lift the working leg outward against the band’s resistance, keeping your core engaged. Slowly return to start and repeat.

lessons.title: Mini-Band Hip Adduction
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Attach a resistance band around your legs above or below the knees, depending on size and tension of band. Stand with feet hip-width apart. Pull your active leg inward toward/across the other leg (standing) . Control the movement back to start.

lessons.title: Bodyweight Hip Hike
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand on one leg on a step or elevated surface, letting the other leg hang. Lower the hanging hip toward the floor, then lift it by engaging your standing leg glutes. Keep movements controlled, focusing on hip stability and strength. Do not 'bounce' between reps - movement to come from the hip, not a 'jump' or push-off with the suspended let.

lessons.title: Banded Crab Walks
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Place a resistance band around your legs above the knees. Stand with feet hip-width apart, slightly bent knees, and a low squat. Step sideways, keeping tension in the band, then step the other foot to follow. Maintain squat position, engaged core, and controlled, continuous movement.

lessons.title: Hip Abduction to Hip Adduction
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand with a resistance band around your legs just above or below the knees. Standing on one leg, move your active leg outward for hip abduction, then pull them back together and across the second leg for hip adduction, controlling the movement and keeping your core engaged throughout.

lessons.title: Double Leg Lying Leg Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your back with legs straight and arms by your sides. Engage core and lift both legs together toward the ceiling, keeping them straight. Slowly lower legs without touching the floor, maintaining tension in abs. Control movement and breathe steadily throughout the exercise.

lessons.title: Seated Double Leg Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Sit upright, back and legs straight, hands by sides or under hips for support. Engage core, and lift both legs together until vertical. Lower slowly without touching ground, keeping movement controlled. Strengthens lower abs, hip flexors, and enhances core stability and control.

lessons.title: Clamshell with Internal Rotation
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your side with knees bent at 90°. Keeping feet together, lift the top knee while rotating it slightly inward, then lower with control to target glutes and hip stabilizers.

lessons.title: Banded Single Leg Lift
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Sit on a mat with a resistance band around your ankles. Keeping your knees straight, lift the one leg and slowly return under tension. Keep core engaged throughout.

lessons.title: Standing Hip Kickbacks
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand up straight with a resistance band around your lower legs. Keeping your core tight, lift one leg straight back behind you and up, squeezing your glutes at the top. Lower slowly and repeat on the other side.

lessons.title: Opening Leg Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Sit on the floor, legs straight, hands by sides or under hips for support. Engage core, and lift one legs until vertical. Move outwards, then lower slowly without touching the ground. Return to first position. Keep movement controlled.

lessons.title: Banded Side Leg Lift
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your side with a resistance band around your thighs. Keep your legs straight and lift the top leg against the band, squeezing your glutes. Lower slowly with control and repeat for the desired reps.

lessons.title: Single Leg Lying Leg Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight. Engage your core and lift the one leg toward the ceiling, keeping it straight. Slowly lower it back down without touching the floor, maintaining control throughout the movement.

lessons.title: Double Hip Circle
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on hips. Move your hips in a wide circular motion clockwise, then repeat counterclockwise. Keep your chest tall and core engaged while tracing big, smooth circles to mobilize the hips and improve flexibility.

lessons.title: Single Leg Sitting Leg Raise
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Sit on the floor with both legs extended. Engage your core and lift the extended leg off the ground slowly, keeping it straight. Lower it back down with control.

lessons.title: Lateral Leg Swings
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand tall and hold onto a support for balance. Swing one leg side to side in a controlled motion, keeping your core engaged and torso stable. Repeat on the other leg to loosen hips and improve mobility.

lessons.title: Single Leg Hip Circles
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Stand using a wall for support if needed, and raise your knee to 90 degrees. Slowly draw small controlled circles in the air with the hip of the raised leg, keeping your core tight and hips stable. Reverse direction, then switch sides to engage hips and lower abs.

lessons.title: Hip CARS
categories: Warm ups: Mobilisations for Individual Muscle Groups
lessons.details: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Lift one knee to the side, rotate it in a circular motion from the hip, keeping core engaged and back stable. Reverse direction. Activates glutes and hip muscles, enhancing mobility, stability, and joint range of motion.

lessons.title: Balance: what is it, and how does it apply to my running?
lessons.details:
Balance is essential for efficient and safe running because each stride is essentially a brief moment of single-leg support. During that moment, the body has to control impact forces, keep the center of mass aligned over the foot, and prepare for the next step. When balance is good, movement stays smooth and controlled, energy is transferred forward instead of sideways, and joints share load more evenly, reducing stress and fatigue.

Runners generally land with a heel strike, midfoot strike, or forefoot strike, and balance plays a key role in how well each works. With a heel strike, balance helps manage the braking forces that occur when the foot lands ahead of the body. Poor balance often leads to overstriding and excess stress on the knee and ankle. With a midfoot strike, the foot lands closer to the body’s center of mass, so balance is critical for maintaining stability and allowing forces to spread evenly through the foot and lower leg. A forefoot strike places even greater demands on balance because the runner must stabilize quickly on the ball of the foot while controlling higher loads through the calf and Achilles. Without good balance, this pattern can lead to overuse injuries.

Balance can be improved through simple running-specific drills that challenge single-leg control. Exercises like strides with controlled form, high knees, skipping, single-leg hops, and running drills that emphasize posture and cadence train the nervous system to stabilize more efficiently. Consistently practicing these drills helps reinforce proper mechanics, improve coordination, and make balanced movement automatic during regular running.

lessons.title: Double Leg Midfoot Balance
lessons.details: Stand tall with your weight centered over the midfoot, heels raised so you can hover with heels approx 1-2 inches over the ground. Keep your core engaged and hips level. Hold this balanced position without leaning forward or back, focusing on stability and alignment through the ankle, knee, and hip.

lessons.title: Double Leg Midfoot Balance Weight Pass
lessons.details: Stand on your MIDFOOT, heels raised, holding a weight in one hand. You should be able to fit a paperback book under your heels to ensure you're on your midfoot. Slowly pass the weight from hand to hand while maintaining balance. Keep your core tight and hips level to challenge stability and coordination.

lessons.title: Runner's Arabesque
lessons.details: Stand on one leg and hinge forward at the hips, extending the other leg straight behind you. Reach your arms forward or out to the sides for balance, keeping your core tight and back flat. Slowly return to upright and repeat on the other leg.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Squat
lessons.details: Stand on a BOSU ball with feet shoulder-width apart, core engaged. Lower into a squat by bending your knees and pushing hips back, keeping chest upright. Drive through your heels to return to standing, maintaining balance throughout the movement.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Hip Stride
lessons.details: Lunge forwards into a hip flexor stretch position, with front foot on the Bosu ball and the other on the floor. Step forward or backward with control, keeping your core engaged and hips level. Focus on balance and smooth movement throughout each stride.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Split Squat
lessons.details: Place your rear foot on a BOSU ball and front foot firmly on the floor. Lower into a split squat by bending your front knee while keeping chest tall. Push through the front heel to rise back up, maintaining balance and control.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Rear Leg Split Squat
lessons.details: Place one foot on the Bosu ball behind you, ball side down, and the other foot firmly on the floor. Lower your back knee toward the ground, keeping your front knee over your ankle. Push through your front heel to return to standing.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Double Leg Calf Raise
lessons.details: Stand with both feet on the Bosu ball, heels hanging off the edge. Rise onto your toes, pause, then lower slowly below the level of the Bosu. Keep your core tight and balance steady throughout the movement.

lessons.title: Bosu Ball Single Leg Calf Raise
lessons.details: Stand on one foot on the Bosu ball, keeping your core tight for balance. Push through your toes to lift your heel, then slowly lower back down. Maintain control and stability throughout the movement.

lessons.title: Skater Bounds (lower body only - balance focus)
lessons.details: Start in a small squat, jump laterally to one side, landing on the opposite leg without swinging your arms for momentum. Absorb impact softly and immediately push off for the next bound. Keep your core tight and maintain balance throughout each jump.

lessons.title: Single Leg Midfoot Balance
lessons.details: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, and lift one leg off the floor. Raise your heel and shift weight onto the ball of your foot, keeping toes grounded. Engage your core, maintain a straight posture, and hold balance without leaning forward or back. Focus on stability and control.

lessons.title: Single Leg Midfoot Balance Weight Pass
lessons.details: Stand on one leg on your MIDFOOT, heel raised, holding a weight in one hand. You should be able to fit a paperback book under your heel to ensure you're on your midfoot. Slowly pass the weight from hand to hand while maintaining balance. Keep your core tight and hips level to challenge stability and coordination.

lessons.title: Skater Bounds
lessons.details: Stand on one leg, then jump laterally to the opposite side, landing softly on the other foot. Swing arms for balance and keep chest tall. Continue bounding side to side with control, engaging glutes, quads, and core for power, stability, and coordination.

lessons.title: Double Hop Skater Bounds
lessons.details: Start on one leg and hop twice in place for control, then bound laterally to the opposite leg. Land softly, stabilize, and repeat with one small hop before the next bound. Keep chest tall, core engaged, and movements smooth to build power, balance, and coordination.

lessons.title: Stride length: what is it, and how does it apply to my running?
lessons.details:
Stride length is half of the stride length times cadence equation that determines running speed, making it key for running economy. Increasing stride length through stronger push-off rather than overreaching allows each step to cover more ground with less energy cost. It relies on hip extension power, ankle stiffness, and horizontal force production, and can be improved with plyometrics, posterior-chain work, and resisted running.

Practicing stride length reinforces proper mechanics under higher forces, but increasing it too quickly carries risks. Overstriding or encouraging heel striking can increase braking forces, joint stress, and the likelihood of injuries such as shin splints, knee pain, or Achilles strain. Gradually lengthening strides at controlled speeds, focusing on midfoot or forefoot contact, helps maintain proper posture and efficiency while supporting faster, sustainable running.

Stride length can be increased safely with mobility work, drills, and progressive on-run practice. Improving hip, ankle, and thoracic range of motion allows greater extension without overload. Drills like high knees, A-skips, and bounding reinforce timing and coordination. Slightly longer strides at controlled speeds let the body adapt gradually while building strength and neuromuscular control for lasting improvements.

lessons.details: Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the ground. Push through your front heel to rise, driving the back knee up explosively toward your chest. Maintain balance and core engagement. Repeat on both sides for strength and stability.

Drive explosively through your legs, swinging your arms forward and jumping onto the box with power and control. Land softly with knees bent, hips back, and chest tall, absorbing the impact through your legs.

Step or jump down under control, depending on your ability and training focus. Reset and repeat with intent.

lessons.details: Start in a small squat, jump laterally to one side, landing on the opposite leg without swinging your arms for momentum. Absorb impact softly and immediately push off for the next bound. Keep your core tight and maintain balance throughout each jump.

lessons.title: Skater Bounds
lessons.details: Stand on one leg, then jump laterally to the opposite side, landing softly on the other foot. Swing arms for balance and keep chest tall. Continue bounding side to side with control, engaging glutes, quads, and core for power, stability, and coordination.

lessons.title: Double Hop Skater Bounds
lessons.details: Start on one leg and hop twice in place for control, then bound laterally to the opposite leg. Land softly, stabilize, and repeat with one small hop before the next bound. Keep chest tall, core engaged, and movements smooth to build power, balance, and coordination.

lessons.title: Single Leg Depth Jump
lessons.details: Step off a box onto one foot, absorb the landing with a soft knee bend, then quickly explode upward into a jump. Maintain balance, stability, and controlled landings before repeating on the other leg.

lessons.title: Single Leg Midfoot Hop
lessons.details: Stand on the balls of your feet with weight centered over your midfoot. Slightly bend knees, then explode upward into a small hop, landing softly on the midfoot. Keep your core engaged and maintain balance throughout. Repeat with controlled, rhythmic jumps.

lessons.title: Single Leg Lateral Hop
lessons.details: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee. Push off that leg to hop laterally, landing softly on the same foot. Maintain balance and control, keeping your core engaged and arms ready for stability. Repeat on the other leg.

lessons.title: Single Leg Ventral Hop
lessons.details: Stand on one leg, bend slightly at the knee, and explosively hop forward. Land softly on the same leg, keeping your core engaged and knee aligned over your foot. Immediately reset and repeat for controlled, powerful forward hops.

lessons.title: Breathing: how do I improve this for running?
lessons.details:
Breathing is important for running because it delivers oxygen to the muscles and removes carbon dioxide. Controlled, rhythmic breathing helps keep the torso stable, maintain posture, and prevent wasted energy from tension or shallow chest movement. Poor breathing can lead to fatigue, inefficient stride mechanics, and side stitches.

Diaphragmatic breathing, which uses the lower lungs, allows deeper, more efficient oxygen exchange. Coordinating breath with stride helps maintain rhythm and balance. A pattern of three steps per inhale and three per exhale is often better than two because it prevents the body from relaxing too much on one side, keeping the torso stable and reducing the risk of side stitches. How you breathe through the nose, mouth, or both depends on the individual. Long, deep inhales followed by shorter exhales can help maintain rhythm and support forward momentum.

Breathing can be improved with drills that focus on core engagement and lung capacity. Controlled strides, hill repeats, and diaphragmatic breathing exercises while trying different breathing patterns help make breathing steady and support smoother, more efficient running.

The RunSpace: Train Smart, Run Stronger.

lessons.title: Running Posture: what is it, and how does it apply to my running?
lessons.details:
Running posture is essential for efficiency, balance, and injury prevention. A tall, relaxed posture allows the spine, hips, and legs to move freely and absorb impact efficiently. Slouching, leaning too far forward, or excessive backward lean can increase strain on the lower back, hips, and legs, reduce stride efficiency, and waste energy.

Good posture relies heavily on core strength. A strong core stabilizes the torso, keeps the chest open, and allows the shoulders to stay relaxed while the head remains aligned with the spine. This alignment supports breathing efficiency, improves balance, and lets the arms swing naturally. Slight adjustments are needed depending on terrain. Uphill running may require a gentle forward lean from the ankles to drive momentum, while downhill running benefits from staying upright and controlled to prevent overstriding or braking with each step.

Posture can be improved through drills that reinforce core engagement and body awareness. Practices like tall strides, hill repeats, and running while focusing on a strong, upright torso help make good posture automatic, reduce fatigue, and support efficient movement. Strong posture also has psychological benefits, helping the runner feel confident, alert, and in control.

The RunSpace: Train Smart, Run Stronger.

lessons.title: Gaze: where to look, and why!
categories: Gaze: where should I look when running, and how does this affect my stride?
lessons.details:
Head position and gaze are critical for running efficiency because they affect posture, balance, and how the body moves with each stride. Keeping the head stable and looking forward helps the spine stay aligned, reduces unnecessary neck and shoulder tension, and allows the torso and legs to move freely. Poor head position, such as looking down or constantly side to side, can cause rounding of the upper back, wasted energy, and strain on the neck and shoulders.

The eyes guide balance and body awareness. Focusing the gaze a few meters ahead rather than directly at the feet helps maintain a natural stride and smooth forward momentum. Looking at the middle distance also has psychological benefits. It helps keep the mind relaxed, reduces anxiety, and allows the runner to anticipate terrain changes without overthinking each step. The head should remain relaxed, not rigid, with minimal up-and-down movement. Adjusting head position slightly with terrain is important. On uphill runs, a small forward tilt can help drive the body forward, while downhill running benefits from a steady gaze that prevents leaning back or overstriding.

Gaze and head control can be improved through drills that emphasize posture and forward focus. Practices like controlled strides, hill repeats, and running with a tall, relaxed posture while keeping the eyes forward help reinforce proper alignment, smooth movement, and a calm, focused mindset.

The RunSpace: Train Smart, Run Stronger.

lessons.title: Arm Drive: What is it, and how does it affect my running?
lessons.details:
Arm drive is important for running efficiency because it helps control rhythm, balance, and forward momentum. The arms counterbalance the legs and stabilize the torso, allowing energy to move forward instead of being lost to rotation or excess movement. Good arm mechanics reduce fatigue and help maintain consistent form, especially as speed increases.

Effective arm drive includes both forward and backward motion, with the back drive being especially important. Driving the elbow back engages the triceps, generating propulsion, maintaining cadence, and preventing the arms from crossing the body. Weak back drive or tricep weakness can lead to wasted energy and poor torso stability. Arm action also adapts to terrain: uphill running requires more forceful, compact swings to lift the body, while downhill running often widens the arms slightly to aid balance and control.

Arm drive can be improved through running drills like high knees, skipping, and short accelerations that emphasize relaxed but powerful arm swings, as well as tricep-strengthening exercises that support a stronger back drive.

lessons.title: Short Mat Stretch Routine (3mins)
lessons.details: A follow-along stretching routine using a mat for after your run (3 minutes).

lessons.title: Runner's Stretch (Hamstrings, Quads & Hip Flexors)
lessons.details: Step one foot forward into a lunge, keeping the back leg extended. Sink hips forward to stretch the hip flexor, bend the front knee slightly to stretch the quadriceps, and hinge at the hips to stretch the hamstrings. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Standing Hamstring Stretch into Calf Stretch
lessons.details: Stand tall, hinge at the hips, and stretch your toes forwards to stretch your hamstrings. From there, tilt your toe upwards to extend the stretch into the calf, pressing your heels into the ground to deepen the calf stretch. Hold each position briefly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.

lessons.title: Quick Full Body Stretch (Standing 4mins)
lessons.details: A quick 4-minute full body stretch requiring no equipment (standing version)

lessons.title: Wall Calf Stretch
lessons.details: Stand facing a wall, place your hands against it, and step one foot back. Keep the back leg straight with the heel pressed into the floor while bending the front knee. Lean forward until you feel a stretch in the calf. Switch sides after holding.

lessons.title: Standing Supported Calf Stretch
lessons.details: Stand facing a wall or sturdy support, place your hands against it, and step one foot back. Keep the back leg straight, heel on the ground, and lean forward to stretch the calf. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Standing Calf Stretch
lessons.details: Stand upright, and step one foot back. Keep the front leg straight, heel pressed into the ground, and lean forward until you feel a stretch in the calf. Extend the stretch by lifting the toe upwards.

lessons.title: Sitting Banded Calf Stretch
lessons.details: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Loop a resistance band around the ball of one foot and hold the ends in your hands. Gently pull the band toward you, flexing your foot to stretch the calf. Keep your leg straight and hold the stretch.

lessons.title: Standing Tibialis Stretch
lessons.details: Stand tall and place the top of one foot behind you on the floor, toes pointing down. Gently press the toes into the ground to stretch the front of your shin (tibialis anterior). Keep posture upright and hold the stretch before switching sides.

lessons.title: Prone Quad Stretch
lessons.details: Lie face down and bend one knee, bringing your heel toward your glutes. Reach back with the same-side hand to hold your ankle, gently pulling it closer to deepen the stretch in the front of your thigh. Keep hips pressed into the floor.

lessons.title: Standing Quad Stretch
lessons.details: Stand tall and pull one ankle toward your glutes, keeping knees together and hips forward. Hold the stretch, then switch legs. Keep your core engaged and back straight.

lessons.title: Banded Quad Stretch
lessons.details: Stand tall and loop a resistance band around one ankle, holding the other end with your hand. Pull the ankle toward your glutes while keeping knees close together and torso upright. Hold the stretch, then switch sides

lessons.title: Banded Hamstring Stretch
lessons.details: Lie on your back with one leg extended and loop a resistance band around the foot. Keep the other leg bent or flat on the floor. Gently pull the band to raise the extended leg, stretching the hamstring. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Standing Hamstring Stretch
lessons.details: Sit or stand and extend one leg forward, keeping it straight. Hinge at the hips and reach toward your toes, feeling a gentle stretch along the back of your thigh. Hold, then switch legs.

lessons.title: Box Glute Stretch
lessons.details: Place one shin across a box or bench with the other leg extended behind you. Hinge forward slightly at the hips while keeping your back straight to feel a deep stretch in the glutes. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Sitting Glute Stretch
lessons.details: Sit on the floor with one leg extended and the other leg bent, crossing the bent leg over the extended one. Hug the bent knee toward your chest to stretch the glutes. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Box Adductor Stretch
lessons.details: Put one leg on a box or chair and bend the opposite leg. Lean forward slightly from the hips, keeping your back straight, to stretch the inner thighs (adductors). Hold, then release.

lessons.title: Standing Piri Formis Stretch
lessons.details: Stand tall and cross one ankle over the opposite knee, forming a “figure 4.” Slowly bend the supporting leg as if sitting into a chair, keeping your chest lifted. Hold the stretch in your outer hip and glutes, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Hip Flexor Stretch 1
lessons.details: Step one foot forward into a lunge position, keeping the back leg straight or slightly bent. Tilt your pelvis under and gently press hips forward, feeling a stretch along the front of the hip. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Sitting Piri Formis Stretch
lessons.details: Sit on a chair with one leg bent and the opposite ankle crossed over the bent knee. Gently push the bent knee away from your chest, keeping back straight, to stretch the piriformis. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Hip Flexor Stretch 2
lessons.details: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, forming a 90-degree angle. Shift hips forward gently, keeping torso upright, until you feel a stretch in the front of the hip. Hold, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Hip Flexors & Piri Formis Stretch
lessons.details: Start in a plank, bring one knee forward, and place it behind your hands with the shin angled. Extend the other leg straight back. Keep hips square and chest tall, then fold forward to stretch hip flexors and piriformis. Hold and breathe deeply.

lessons.title: Adductor Stretch
lessons.details: Stand with feet wide apart, then bend one knee while keeping the other leg straight. Shift your weight toward the bent knee to feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg. Hold and repeat on the other side.

lessons.title: Sitting Groin Stretch
lessons.details: Sit on the floor with the soles of your feet pressed together and knees bent outward. Hold your feet with your hands and gently press your knees toward the ground to feel the stretch in your groin and inner thighs. Keep your back tall.

lessons.title: Squatting Groin Stretch
lessons.details: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and squat down, keeping your chest upright. Place your elbows inside your knees and press them outward gently to open your hips. Hold the stretch and breathe deeply.

lessons.title: Child's Pose
lessons.details: Kneel on the floor, touch your big toes together, and sit back on your heels. Extend your arms forward and lower your chest toward the ground, resting your forehead down. Breathe deeply, relaxing through your hips, back, and shoulders.

lessons.title: Posterior Chain Stretch
lessons.details: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hinge at the hips, and reach hands toward the floor while keeping legs straight but not locked. Feel the stretch along your hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. Hold while keeping your spine long and core engaged.

lessons.title: Cat Cow
lessons.details: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Inhale, arch your back, drop your belly, and lift your chest and tailbone (Cow). Exhale, round your spine, tuck your chin and tailbone (Cat). Flow smoothly between both positions with controlled breathing.

lessons.title: Runner's Stretch with Core Rotation
lessons.details: Step one foot forward into a lunge, keeping the back leg straight. Rotate your torso toward the front leg while extending the opposite arm upward. Hold the stretch, engaging your core, then switch sides.

lessons.title: Back Stretch
lessons.details: Start in a high plank, then lift your hips up and back, forming an inverted V shape. Press your heels toward the floor, relax your head between your arms, and lengthen your spine to stretch your back, hamstrings, and calves.

lessons.title: Foam Rolling: Calves
lessons.details: Sit on a foam roller placed under your calves. Divide your calves into 3 areas - side, side, and back - and spend 1-2 minutes on each area. Support your weight with your hands behind you, roll slowly from just below your knees to your ankles, pausing on tight spots to release tension. Don't roll the joints! To increase the tension, press down with your other leg - for less tension, support your weight through your hands more.

lessons.title: Foam Rolling: Glutes
lessons.details: Sit on a foam roller placed under your glutes. Divide your glutes into 2 areas - side, and back - and spend 1-2 minutes on each area. Support your weight with your hands behind you, roll slowly from just above your knees to your glutes, pausing on tight spots to release tension. To increase the tension, use less support from your other leg - for less tension, support your weight through your hands and opposite leg more.

lessons.title: Foam Rolling: Hamstrings
lessons.details: Sit on a foam roller placed under your hamstrings. Divide your hamstrings into 3 areas - side, side, and back - and spend 1-2 minutes on each area. Support your weight with your hands behind you, roll slowly from just above your knees to your glutes, pausing on tight spots to release tension. To increase the tension, press down with your other leg - for less tension, support your weight through your hands more.
